How to type an API response safely

Generated types are a description of the samples you gave the generator, not a promise about the API. They are still the fastest way to a correct first draft, as long as you know where they lie.

Optional is not nullable

CaseIn the JSONTypeScript
OptionalThe key is sometimes absentname?: string
NullableThe key is present with nullname: string | null
BothAbsent in some, null in othersname?: string | null

A single sample can show neither. That is why the tool asks for several samples and warns when you give it one: every field of a one-sample type is marked required.

Pick samples that disagree

  • A record with every field filled, and one with as many as possible empty.
  • A list with items and the same list empty (an empty array has no item type).
  • An error response, if your code receives them on the same path.

Types vanish at runtime: validate at the edge

TypeScript types are erased when the code runs, so a response that no longer matches fails somewhere far from the cause. The Zod output gives you a schema to parse the response with, and an inferred type from the same definition, so the check and the type cannot drift apart.

What the tool guesses, and flags

  • Strings that are always ISO dates, UUIDs, emails or URLs are annotated; one odd value turns the annotation off.
  • An object with many ID-like keys becomes a map instead of one field per ID.
  • Fields that hold more than one type are listed so you can check they are intended.
  • Whole numbers stay integers until a decimal shows up. A price that happens to be 10 in your sample may be 10.5 tomorrow.

Using the generator

Paste the samples into the tool or run node cli.mjs a.json b.json --style zod, read the notes it prints, and commit the result. Re-run it when the API changes.

No warranty. Provided free and as-is. This is general information about typing practice, not professional advice. Best-effort hosting, no SLA. The page makes no network calls and uploads nothing. Generate types from JSON.

JSON TO TYPES GENERATOR · RUNS IN YOUR BROWSER

Turn JSON into TypeScript, Zod, JSON Schema or Go

Paste an API response, or several, and get types that match what the API really returns: optional fields found by merging samples, nullable fields, integers versus floats, dates, UUIDs, emails and URLs recognised, and identical nested shapes shared.

Nothing is uploaded. Your JSON stays in this tab and the page makes no network calls.

Your JSON

One value, several samples one per line (NDJSON), or several objects pasted back to back. More samples means better optional and nullable detection.

Paste JSON and click Generate.

Generated code

Run it on files from the command line

node cli.mjs response.json                       # TypeScript
node cli.mjs a.json b.json c.json --style zod    # merge three samples
cat samples.ndjson | node cli.mjs --style go --name ApiResponse
node cli.mjs data.json --style jsonschema --readonly

Get cli.mjs and types.mjs from the repo. Node 18+, no dependencies.

Common questions

How do I generate TypeScript types from JSON?

Paste a JSON response, or several samples, and pick TypeScript. The tool reads every sample, merges them, and writes one interface per object shape. Fields missing from some samples become optional, fields that are sometimes null become nullable, and strings that are always dates, UUIDs, emails or URLs are annotated.

Why paste more than one sample?

One sample cannot show which fields are optional or which values can be null, so every field comes out required. Paste several responses one after another, or one per line, and the merged types reflect what the API actually returns.

Which output formats are supported?

TypeScript interfaces, Zod schemas with inferred types, JSON Schema (draft 2020-12), and Go structs with json tags. All four come from the same inferred model.

Does this upload my JSON?

No. Everything runs in this page and the page makes no network calls, so API responses containing customer data stay on your device. The CLI reads files or stdin on your machine and prints to your terminal.

How is this different from quicktype or json2ts?

It overlaps on purpose. It merges many samples, reports what it had to guess, and needs no install, account or upload. For a build-time pipeline use a maintained generator; use this to get a correct first draft in seconds.
